headline: Kanshin is 関 (kan, “concern”) plus 心 (shin, “heart”).

sources.quote: From 関 (kan, “concern”) + 心 (shin, “heart”).

headline: Hakase is ultimately from Middle Chinese 博士, an official title in the ritsuryō system, likely borrowed in the Old Japanese period.

sources.quote: Ultimately from Middle Chinese 博士 (pak dzri^X). Unattested in extant Old Japanese texts, but likely borrowed in the Old Japanese period, being an official title in the ritsuryō system.

headline: Kōsha is 校 (kō, “school”) plus 舎 (-sha, “house”), first attested in 1884.

sources.quote: Compound of 校(こう) (kō, “school”) + 舎(しゃ) (-sha, “house”).
First attested in 1884.

headline: Ke, “hair”, is cognate with Proto-Ryukyuan *ke (“hair, fur”).

sources.quote: From Old Japanese. Attested in the Man'yōshū of circa 759 CE. Ultimately from Proto-Japonic *kay. Cognate with Proto-Ryukyuan *ke (“hair, fur”).

headline: Kangofu is 看護 (“nursing”) plus 婦 (“woman; female”).

sources.quote: Compound of 看護 (“nursing”) + 婦 (“woman; female”).

pos: noun or participle which takes the aux. verb suru
headline: Chōsa is chō (調, investigate) plus sa (査, look into).

sources.quote: From chō (調, investigate) + sa (査, look into).

headline: Sore is そ (so, “that”, medial reference marker) plus れ (-re, specific pronoun referent marker).

sources.quote: Compound of そ (so, “that”, medial reference marker) + れ (-re, specific pronoun referent marker).

headline: Yane is 屋 (ya, “building, house”) plus 根 (ne, “root”), and ancient houses were dugouts where the roof came right down to the ground.

sources.quote: 屋(や) (ya, “building, house”) + 根(ね) (ne, “root”).
Houses in ancient Japan were dugouts, where the roof came right down to the ground.

headline: Chigai is the continuative stem of 違う (chigau, “to differ”).

sources.quote: 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 違(ちが)う (chigau, “to differ”).
Formed from 違(ちが)う (chigau, “to differ”).

headline: Tōri is the stem form of 通る (tōru, “to go by; to go past; to go along”).

sources.quote: From the 連用形 (ren'yōkei, “stem form”) of the verb 通る (tōru, “to go by; to go past; to go along”, intransitive).

pos: nouns which may take the genitive case particle 'no'
headline: Sekidō is an orthographic borrowing from Chinese 赤道 (chìdào).

sources.quote: Orthographic borrowing from Chinese 赤道 (chìdào).

meaning: to suffer, to groan, to be worried
headline: Kurushimu is first cited to the Kojiki of 712 CE, related to 苦しい (kurushii, “painful, suffering”).

sources.quote: From Old Japanese. First cited to the Kojiki of 712 CE and related to 苦しい (kurushii, “painful, suffering”). See that entry for more details.
-mu is an auxiliary suffix of becoming the specified state.

headline: Butsu is a shift from 打つ (utsu).

sources.quote: Shift from 打(う)つ (utsu).

meaning: to bet, to risk, to gamble
headline: Kakeru, “to bet”, is derived from 掛ける (kakeru, “to hang; to manipulate; to spend, invest”).

sources.quote: Derived from 掛(か)ける (kakeru, “to hang; to manipulate; to spend, invest”).

headline: Atsukamashii is related to 厚い (atsui, “thick”).

sources.quote: Related to 厚い (atsui, “thick”).

pos: noun or participle which takes the aux. verb suru
headline: Setsubi appears to be a Meiji-period repurposing of written Chinese 設備 (shèbèi, “equipment; to make preparations”) and Old Japanese 設け備ふ (makesonapu).

sources.quote: Appears to be a Meiji period repurposing or borrowing, probably based on written Chinese 設備 /设备 (shèbèi, “equipment; to make preparations and arrangements”) and Old Japanese 設け備ふ (makesonapu), modernized classical Japanese 設け備う (makesonau, “to arrange in preparation”).
First attested in a pocket English–Japanese dictionary from 1862, provided as the gloss for the verb season, presumably from the sense of "to make something ready".

headline: Nichiyōhin is, by surface analysis, 日用 (nichiyō, “everyday use”) plus 品 (-hin, “item”).

sources.quote: By surface analysis, 日用(にちよう) (nichiyō, “everyday use”) + 品(ひん) (-hin, “item”).

meaning: to seize, to catch, to grasp
headline: Tsukamu is derived from 束 (tsuka, “bunch, bundle”) plus -mu, and is first cited to a text from 850.

sources.quote: Derived from 束 (tsuka, “bunch, bundle”) + む (-mu, verb-forming suffix indicating “to look like, to seem like”).
First cited to a text from 850.

headline: Kurīmu is English cream, a doublet of クレーム (kurēmu).

sources.quote: From English cream. Doublet of クレーム (kurēmu).

headline: Jidōsha is 自動 (jidō, “automatic movement”) plus 車 (-sha, “vehicle”).

sources.quote: From 自動(じどう) (jidō, “automatic movement”) + 車(しゃ) (-sha, “vehicle”).

headline: Geijutsu is from Literary Chinese 藝術, collectively the 六藝 (Liùyì, “Six Arts”) and 術數 (shùshù, “numerology”).

sources.quote: From Literary Chinese 藝術, collectively the 六藝 (Liùyì, “Six Arts”) and 術數 (shùshù, “numerology”)

headline: Taira is た (ta-) plus 平 (hira), attested in the Nihon Shoki (720 CE).

sources.quote: た (ta-) + 平 (hira).

Attested in the Nihon Shoki (720 CE). The Ruiju Myōgishō (late Heian period) gives two readings for 平, タヒラ (tahira, modern taira) and タヒラカ (tahiraka); it is not clear whether the two had different meanings.

headline: Ashiato is 足 (ashi, “foot”) plus 跡 (ato, “trace, mark”).

sources.quote: 足(あし) (ashi, “foot”) + 跡(あと) (ato, “trace, mark”)

headline: Nagai is first attested in the Kojiki of 712 CE, and is possibly cognate with 流れる (nagareru, “to flow”), in reference to extending.

sources.quote: From Old Japanese. First attested in the Kojiki of 712 CE. From Proto-Japonic *nanka.
Possibly cognate with 流れる (nagareru, “to flow”, intransitive), and 流す (nagasu, “to flow”, transitive), in reference to extending.

headline: Setsu, “theory”, is from Middle Chinese 說.

sources.quote: From Middle Chinese 說 (MC sywet).

headline: Kinzoku is Middle Chinese 金屬, literally “metal + be attached to; category”.

sources.quote: From Middle Chinese compound 金屬 /金属 (kim dzyowk, literally “metal + be attached to; category”).

headline: Zairyō is a Middle Chinese compound, literally “materials + ingredients”.

sources.quote: From Middle Chinese compound 材料 (dzoj lewᴴ, literally “materials + ingredients”). Compare modern Mandarin reading cáiliào.

headline: Botchan is 坊 (bō) plus ちゃん (-chan).

sources.quote: 坊(ぼう) (bō) + ちゃん (-chan)

headline: Kado, “corner”, is from Old Japanese, from Proto-Japonic *kanto.

sources.quote: From Old Japanese, in turn, from Proto-Japonic *kanto.

headline: Irasshai is the imperative of いらっしゃる (irassharu), shortened from いらっしゃいまし (irasshaimashi).

sources.quote: Imperative form (命(めい)令(れい)形(けい) (meireikei)) of いらっしゃる (irassharu); shortening of いらっしゃいまし (irasshaimashi).

pos: noun or participle which takes the aux. verb suru
headline: Shōka is from Middle Chinese 消化 (MC sjew xwaeH).

sources.quote: From Middle Chinese 消化 (MC sjew xwaeH).
